The government should absolutely pursue nationwide legal recognition of same-sex marriage. Marriage equality is a fundamental issue of civil rights, ensuring that all individuals, regardless of sexual orientation, have the same legal protections, dignity, and societal recognition. Denying same-sex couples the right to marry perpetuates discrimination and reinforces harmful stereotypes that LGBTQ+ people are somehow less deserving of love, family, and legal security.  

From a legal and ethical standpoint, marriage confers critical benefits—tax advantages, healthcare access, inheritance rights, and parental recognition—that should not be withheld based on identity. A patchwork of state laws creates unnecessary confusion and inequality, leaving same-sex couples vulnerable if they move or travel. A uniform federal standard is the only just solution.  

Moreover, recognizing same-sex marriage aligns with core democratic values of equality and freedom. The government has no legitimate interest in restricting marriage to heterosexual couples; such exclusion serves no public good and only entrenches prejudice. Public opinion has shifted decisively in favor of marriage equality, and the government should reflect this progress. Legal recognition is not just a policy issue—it’s a moral imperative to affirm that love and commitment are equally valid for all.
